cues.en: Mike: I have mentioned before the term "expected value" in this course.
cues.zh: Mike：這門課之前提過「期望值」這個詞。

cues.en: In particular, I mentioned it when I introduced you to the mean, and I said that the mean is not the same thing as the expected value.
cues.zh: 尤其在介紹平均值時，說過平均值和期望值不一樣。

cues.en: And so, in this video, I'm going to tell you what expected value means, and we will also point out some differences between expected value and the average.
cues.zh: 這部影片會解釋期望值的意義，也會指出期望值和平均值的一些差異。

cues.en: And I'll give you the definition, we'll go through an example, and I'll also give a bit of a geometric interpretation of expected value.
cues.zh: 會給出定義、看一個例子，也會稍微從幾何角度解讀期望值。

cues.en: Now, in this video, I'm going to ask you to pause the video a couple of times, I think it's two times or maybe three times, and do a little bit of math yourself.
cues.zh: 這部影片會請你暫停幾次，我想是兩次或三次，自己做一點數學計算。

cues.en: So get ready, I hope you have a piece of paper and a pencil at hand.
cues.zh: 準備好，希望手邊有紙筆。

cues.en: All right, so here we have the formulas for the average, which you've already seen before, and expected value.
cues.zh: 這裡是之前看過的平均值公式，以及期望值公式。

cues.en: So expected value is typically indicated with a capital E.
cues.zh: 期望值通常用大寫 E 表示。

cues.en: And then in square brackets like this, you would have the variable, or the sample, that you are computing the expected value of.
cues.zh: 後面像這樣加上中括號，裡面放要計算期望值的變數或樣本。

cues.en: Okay, so let's see.
cues.zh: 好，看看。

cues.en: So i refers to the index.
cues.zh: i 代表索引。

cues.en: So Xi is the ith index in dataset X.
cues.zh: 所以 Xᵢ 是資料集 X 中第 i 個索引位置的值。

cues.en: N is the total number of elements.
cues.zh: N 是元素總數。

cues.en: And P-sub-i is the probability of observing data value X.
cues.zh: p 下標 i，是觀察到資料值 X 的機率。

cues.en: So, here's a question: When are these two formulas equal?
cues.zh: 問題是，這兩個公式何時相等？

cues.en: In other words, when is expected value and average the same thing?
cues.zh: 換句話說，期望值和平均值何時是同一回事？

cues.en: So I'd like you to pause the video, if you need to, and figure this out, when are these two formulas equal?
cues.zh: 如果需要，暫停影片，想想這兩個公式何時相等。

cues.en: Well, these two formulas are equal when P equals one over N.
cues.zh: 當 p=1/N 時，這兩個公式相等。

cues.en: And what does that mean?
cues.zh: 這代表什麼？

cues.en: Well, that means that all of the data values are equally likely to occur.
cues.zh: 代表所有資料值出現的可能性相同。

cues.en: We are just as likely to get, you know, whatever X1 is, and X2, and X3, up to XN.
cues.zh: 不管 X₁、X₂、X₃，一直到 Xₙ 是什麼，得到它們的機會都相同。

cues.en: All these values are equally likely to occur in the data.
cues.zh: 所有值出現在資料中的可能性相同。

cues.en: And that gives us that the probability of any given event is one over N.
cues.zh: 因此，任何特定事件的機率就是 1/N。

cues.en: And that means that the expected value is the same thing as X-bar, which is the average.
cues.zh: 這表示，期望值和 X 上橫線，也就是平均值相同。

cues.en: So this is what I call the obvious difference between average and expected value, because we're just reading it from the formula.
cues.zh: 我把這稱為平均值和期望值之間明顯的差異，因為直接從公式就看得出來。

cues.en: So let's make that more clear.
cues.zh: 再說清楚一點。

cues.en: So the average is an empirical sample estimate based on a finite amount of data, so that is the average.
cues.zh: 平均值是根據有限資料得到的經驗樣本估計。

cues.en: We just take a sample of data and we, you know, just apply the formula to compute the average, which is we sum up all the data values and divide by N.
cues.zh: 只要取一個資料樣本，套用公式，也就是將所有資料值加總再除以 N，就能計算平均值。

cues.en: Expected value, which is also sometimes called the expectation value, is the expected average in a population.
cues.zh: 期望值，有時也稱 expectation value，是母體中預期的平均值。

cues.en: This is something you could get from knowing something about the population, or from a very, very, very, very large number of samples, so approaching infinity.
cues.zh: 可以根據對母體的某些知識，或非常非常大量、趨近無限的樣本取得。

cues.en: If you start to measure an infinity number, an infinite number of samples, then the expectation would converge with the mean.
cues.zh: 如果開始測量無限多個樣本，期望值就會和平均值收斂在一起。

cues.en: All right, so let's go through an example to make this a little bit more clear.
cues.zh: 用個例子，讓這更清楚。

cues.en: We're gonna make more clear the distinction between the expected value and the sample average.
cues.zh: 進一步釐清期望值和樣本平均值的差異。

cues.en: So here we have an "illegal" die.
cues.zh: 這裡有個「不合法」的骰子。

cues.en: This is a weighted die, and it's illegal because the probabilities of getting different faces, different numbers, is not all equal.
cues.zh: 這是加權骰子，說它不合法，是因為擲出不同面、不同數字的機率不全相等。

cues.en: So we have, the probability of rolling a one is a quarter.
cues.zh: 擲出 1 的機率為四分之一。

cues.en: The probability of rolling a two is a quarter.
cues.zh: 擲出 2 的機率為四分之一。

cues.en: And the probability of all these other sides are one over eight.
cues.zh: 其他各面的機率都是八分之一。

cues.en: Now, first of all, it's useful to do a really quick sanity check and make sure that all these probabilities really add up to one.
cues.zh: 首先，快速做個合理性檢查，確保所有機率總和真的為 1，很有幫助。

cues.en: This is all the possible events that can happen when we roll a die.
cues.zh: 這是擲骰子所有可能發生的事件。

cues.en: Of course we're excluding the ginormously unlikely, though I suppose technically possible, possibility that it just lands on a corner, like this.
cues.zh: 當然排除那種極其不可能，但技術上也許可能，像這樣停在角上的情況。

cues.en: So these are all the possible values.
cues.zh: 所以這些是所有可能值。

cues.en: They're all exclusive.
cues.zh: 它們全都互斥。

cues.en: You can't get a one and a two at the same time.
cues.zh: 不能同時擲出 1 和 2。

cues.en: So that's good, we can really talk about the probability mass distribution of this die.
cues.zh: 很好，可以談這個骰子的機率質量分布。

cues.en: So then we need to make sure that these all add up to one.
cues.zh: 接著確保它們加起來為 1。

cues.en: So a quarter and a quarter is a half.
cues.zh: 四分之一加四分之一等於二分之一。

cues.en: And here, adding these things up, we get four eighths, which is also a half.
cues.zh: 這些加起來是八分之四，也等於二分之一。

cues.en: So then we get to one.
cues.zh: 所以合計為 1。

cues.en: Okay, so here is the question: What is the expected value of this die?
cues.zh: 問題是，這個骰子的期望值是多少？

cues.en: So you roll the die and you get some number, what is the expected value of this die?
cues.zh: 擲骰子會得到某個數字，這個骰子的期望值是多少？

cues.en: So I would like you to pause the video and compute the expected value of this die.
cues.zh: 請暫停影片，計算這個骰子的期望值。

cues.en: And here I'm just showing you the formula in case you need a bit of a reminder.
cues.zh: 這裡也顯示公式，讓你複習。

cues.en: Okay, so did you get it?
cues.zh: 好，算出來了嗎？

cues.en: The answer is that we compute this by literally just writing out this formula here.
cues.zh: 答案就是直接把公式寫出來計算。

cues.en: So we have, the Xs are the values of the sides, and the probabilities are listed here.
cues.zh: X 是各面的數值，機率列在這裡。

cues.en: So we have one times the probability of side one, plus two times the probability of side two, plus blah, blah, blah, up to six times the probability of six.
cues.zh: 1 乘以擲出 1 的機率，加上 2 乘以擲出 2 的機率，依此類推，直到 6 乘以擲出 6 的機率。

cues.en: So that is one over four, plus two over four, plus three over eight.
So I'm just, you know, writing out this equation here.
cues.zh: 只是把這個方程式寫出來。

cues.en: And that gives us an expected value of three.
cues.zh: 得到期望值 3。

cues.en: So the expected value of this die is three.
cues.zh: 所以這個骰子的期望值為 3。

cues.en: Now, notice we didn't actually collect a single data point to compute this expected value.
cues.zh: 注意，計算期望值時，沒有實際收集任何一個資料點。

cues.en: We can compute this expected value knowing all the probabilities of all the possibilities.
cues.zh: 只要知道所有可能結果的機率，就能計算期望值。

cues.en: So no data was required to compute the expected value.
cues.zh: 所以計算期望值不需要資料。

cues.en: Now, that's quite different from computing an average.
cues.zh: 這和計算平均值很不同。

cues.en: To compute the average of a sample, we actually need some sample data.
cues.zh: 計算樣本平均值，確實需要樣本資料。

cues.en: So let's imagine we roll this die, it's a loaded die, we roll it eight times, and here are the answers.
cues.zh: 假設擲這個加權骰子八次，結果如下。

cues.en: Now you can pause the video again and compute the average of this sample.
cues.zh: 現在可以再次暫停影片，計算這個樣本的平均值。

cues.en: So it turns out that the average is 3.25.
cues.zh: 結果平均值是 3.25。

cues.en: It's fairly, you know, takes a minute to compute, but it's a really straightforward operation, you just add up all these numbers, divide by eight.
cues.zh: 可能要花一分鐘，但運算非常直接，把所有數字相加，再除以 8。

cues.en: So the average of this sample is 3.25, but the expected value is exactly the same.
cues.zh: 所以樣本平均值是 3.25，但期望值完全相同。

cues.en: So here you see an example where the expected value is different from the average.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到，期望值和平均值不同的例子。

cues.en: Now, obviously, if you would roll this die again another eight times, you could get 3.25 again, but, you know, it seems likely that you would get some other value.
cues.zh: 顯然，如果再擲八次，可能又得到 3.25，但也很可能得到其他值。

cues.en: Maybe you'd get three or four, you know, you might get 2.75.
cues.zh: 也許是 3 或 4，也可能是 2.75。

cues.en: There's a whole range of possible values you could get.
cues.zh: 有一整個範圍的可能值。

cues.en: And now you can also imagine that if you would repeat this experiment of rolling the die eight times and computing the average, if you repeat that experiment
cues.zh: 現在可以想像，如果重複這個擲八次骰子並計算平均值的實驗，

cues.en: many, many, many, many times, maybe dozens of times, or hundreds, maybe even thousands of times, you would expect that the average of those sample averages, right?
cues.zh: 重複非常非常多次，也許數十次、數百次，甚至數千次，就會預期這些樣本平均值的平均，對吧？

cues.en: Remember, in the previous lecture video, so I guess it was two videos ago, I talked about sampling variability and creating sample estimate distributions.
cues.zh: 記得前一堂影片，應該是前兩部影片，談過抽樣變異，以及建立樣本估計值分布。

cues.en: So you would expect that eventually this number would converge to this number, but they are not necessarily the same.
cues.zh: 可以預期，最後這個數字會收斂到這個數字，但它們不一定相同。

cues.en: And furthermore, just as a quick reminder, the expected value we can compute, knowing only the probabilities, we don't actually need a single data point to compute expected value,
cues.zh: 此外，快速提醒，只要知道機率就能算期望值，不需要任何一個資料點，

cues.en: whereas to compute the average, we do need data.
cues.zh: 但計算平均值就確實需要資料。

cues.en: Okay, so when do you think the expected value and the average are the same?
cues.zh: 好，你認為期望值和平均值何時相同？

cues.en: When do they converge?
cues.zh: 何時收斂？

cues.en: And I unfortunately already just told you the answer in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，上一張投影片已經把答案說出來了。

cues.en: I was a little too enthusiastic about that.
cues.zh: 我有點太興奮。

cues.en: So the answer is that expected value and average converge when drawing large and representative random samples from a population, or repeated samples,
cues.zh: 答案是，從母體抽取大且具代表性的隨機樣本，或重複抽樣時，期望值和平均值會收斂，

cues.en: so a large number of representative random samples from a population.
cues.zh: 也就是從母體取得大量具代表性的隨機樣本。

cues.en: Okay, now I want to give you a bit of a geometric interpretation of the expected value.
cues.zh: 現在從幾何角度解讀期望值。

cues.en: You can think of expected value as like the balance point of a probability distribution.
cues.zh: 可以把期望值想成機率分布的平衡點。

cues.en: So let's imagine we have a probability distribution that looks like this.
cues.zh: 假設機率分布長這樣。

cues.en: So it's skewed to the right.
cues.zh: 向右偏斜。

cues.en: It looks sort of Gaussian in this range, but then it has a large skew to the right.
cues.zh: 這段有點像高斯，但右側有很大的偏斜。

cues.en: So the expected value is basically gonna be like the point on this distribution, the point on the X-axis, where the weight of the distribution
cues.zh: 期望值基本上就是分布上，也就是 X 軸上的某個點，讓分布的重量

cues.en: would be balanced to the left and to the right.
cues.zh: 在左右兩側達到平衡。

cues.en: One way to think about this is, if you take a spoon, so you can do this after the video, go to the kitchen and get a spoon.
cues.zh: 可以這樣想，拿一把湯匙，影片結束後可以到廚房拿。

cues.en: And if someone looks at you weird, tell 'em you're doing science.
cues.zh: 如果有人奇怪地看你，就說在做科學研究。

cues.en: So it's okay, you're doing a scientific experiment.
cues.zh: 所以沒關係，你在做科學實驗。

cues.en: Balance a spoon on your finger.
cues.zh: 把湯匙放在手指上保持平衡。

cues.en: And the question is, where is the balance point?
cues.zh: 問題是，平衡點在哪裡？

cues.en: It's not going to be exactly halfway across the spoon in terms of length.
cues.zh: 不會恰好在湯匙長度的正中間。

cues.en: So where you have to balance that spoon is gonna be closer to the, I don't know what it's called, the head of the spoon?
cues.zh: 平衡湯匙的位置會更接近，我不知道怎麼稱呼，湯匙的頭？

cues.en: The cup of the spoon?
cues.zh: 湯匙的碗部？

cues.en: The scooping part of the spoon?
cues.zh: 湯匙舀東西的部分？

cues.en: Than it is towards the handle of the spoon.
cues.zh: 而不是接近湯匙柄。

cues.en: So that's the way to think about expected value.
cues.zh: 這就是理解期望值的方式。

cues.en: You have a probability distribution, and the expected value is the point on the X-axis where you would balance this probability distribution
cues.zh: 有一個機率分布，而期望值是 X 軸上能讓這個分布平衡的位置，

cues.en: so that it's even on the left and on the right.
cues.zh: 使左右兩側平衡。

cues.en: So here's just an example.
cues.zh: 這裡只是個例子。

cues.en: If you're a little bit too far to the right, it's gonna tip over this way.
cues.zh: 如果太靠右，就會往這邊倒。

cues.en: And if you're too far to the left, it's gonna tip over to the right because there's too much weight on this side.
cues.zh: 如果太靠左，就會往右倒，因為這邊重量太多。

cues.en: So you wanna find this balance point, and that is the expected value.
cues.zh: 所以要找到這個平衡點，那就是期望值。

cues.en: So it's kind of like the geometric graphical intuition of expected value.
cues.zh: 這算是期望值的幾何、圖像直覺。

cues.en: So, in this video, I told you about the difference between expected value and the average, or the mean.
cues.zh: 這部影片介紹了期望值和平均值，也就是 mean 的差異。

cues.en: And I guess the way to think about it is that expected value is a bit of a theoretical concept, and the average is an empirical concept.
cues.zh: 可以想成，期望值比較偏理論概念，而平均值是經驗概念。
